terms.comment: Our phrase, like mēnsa pōmāria, the fruit stall: mēnsa is the classical word for the table goods are sold from (Lewis & Short: “a market-stand for meat, vegetables, etc.”), and piscātōrius is classical (forum piscātōrium, the fish market, Col. 8.17.15, in Lewis & Short). Traupman has the fish market, forum piscārium (pp. 174, 316); neither he nor Morgan–Owens has a word for a fish stall.

sources: Theodōrus et pater · Ad Larem avītum, Libellī I–VII, as they stood on 7 November 2026, with their glosses. Examples marked “Libellus” quote those texts word for word; classical passages are cited by author.
Lewis & Short: mensa · Lewis & Short: piscatorius
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 174, 316.
